ops.title: cc-transcript CI test(3.13) red on main: command-parse parity fails on ubuntu
ops.premise: The test (3.13) job on ubuntu-latest has failed identically on every main run since at least 2026-07-20 (commits 5d35022, bafe6ff, 7a66e02, 56ee824, 106b603, dadcda0, d5258dc) in tests/test_command.py + tests/test_command_parity.py + tests/test_splice_parity.py, while the same suite passes on macOS — suspected fallout of the tree-sitter-bash → rable parser swap (a3c57df): either a Linux-vs-macOS parse divergence in rable, or goldens/tests never regenerated for the new command_parse schema, with a platform-conditional dependency resolution explaining the local/CI split.

ops.text: Failure signature (runs 29740515472 on 2026-07-20 and 29916869341 on 2026-07-22, byte-identical): test_multiple_redirects expects raw stripped of trailing redirects ('echo hello') but native returns the full raw ('echo hello >> out.txt 2>&1'); while/loop/if/heredoc command_prefixes return () where nonempty tuples expected; command/splice parity goldens are shaped {'parts': [...]} while _native.command_parse emits {'raw','executable','args','redirects','prefixes',...}.

The swift job (macos-15) is green on the same commits, and the full local pytest suite passes on macOS (exit 0, 2026-07-21) — the break is ubuntu-only or environment-conditional, not a plain stale-golden situation, since stale goldens would fail on macOS too.
d5258dc (blame/attribute feature push) touches none of the failing subsystem; its CI red is blocked-by-preexisting-breakage.
